historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr). FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding - interest income): FY2020 832.0, FY2021 583.7, FY2022 426.4, FY2023 981.2, FY2024 946.1, FY2025 1,010.8 (withholding only available FY2023 onward, $22.8M/$42.1M/$57.2M). The 3-year figures compound off the FY2022 inventory-build trough and are not a run-rate. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (4.0%) is well below reported FCF (7.5%) because interest income ($37M -> $129M) and SBC + withholding ($81M -> $223M) grew far faster than cash flow; equity, revenue and EPS 5yr CAGRs agree within 30%, so no divergence flag. The base driver path starts at guidance (11.1%) and decelerates to 3% by year 10, below the 10.2% selected rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance year delivered, then a normal maturing of a hardware franchise: growth decelerates from 11% to 3% over ten years, pre-SBC EBITDA margin flat at ~32%, capex and working capital normalise. Auto OEM's H2 2026 dip is bridged by the 2027 Mercedes-Benz programme; tariffs stay at the 10% baseline assumed in guidance.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fitness becomes a mass-market health platform rather than an athlete niche, recurring software (Connect+, TrainingPeaks) lifts mix, Marine/Aviation stay double-digit and Auto OEM turns profitable on Mercedes-Benz; margin expands to 34% and growth stays high-single-digit into the 2030s.
scenario_narratives.bear: Post-2026 the Fitness cycle exhausts, tariffs escalate above 10% on Taiwan assembly, big-ticket Marine/Aviation demand softens with rates, and the Auto OEM programme gap widens; revenue flat-lines for two years and the margin gives back the FY2024-26 expansion.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Garmin is a debt-free, net-cash hardware compounder whose reported FCF flatters owner economics on two counts: ~$129M of interest on a $4.4B securities pile that is separately added back in the bridge, and ~$223M of SBC plus withholding. On owner FCF the business earned ~$1.0B in FY2025 against a ~$57B market cap, so the current price capitalises the FY2026 margin step-up and a long runway of Fitness-led growth. The valuation therefore turns on how long double-digit Fitness growth persists and whether the 27% operating margin survives tariffs and component inflation; the model treats 32% pre-SBC EBITDA as the steady state and lets growth fade to 3%.
key_risks_to_valuation: US tariff escalation on Taiwan-assembled products beyond the 10% baseline embedded in guidance (~25% of revenue exposed)
Fitness growth mean-reverting from 25-40% to single digits as the wearables upgrade cycle matures and Apple/Coros/Suunto/Chinese entrants compress the niche
Auto OEM revenue gap in H2 2026-2027 between the BMW programme peak and the Mercedes-Benz ramp, with historically loss-making segment economics
Rate-sensitive Marine and Aviation demand (boats, GA aircraft) rolling over in a weaker consumer/business spending environment
Memory and component cost inflation flagged by management for late 2026 eroding the guided margin expansion
Working-capital intensity: inventory and receivables have consumed $180-380M a year of cash, so slower growth releases cash but faster growth costs more than the margin suggests
Terminal value is ~55-60% of enterprise value; a 1pp move in WACC or terminal growth moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $166.003M plus 'Purchase of treasury shares related to equity awards' $57.194M (financing; net-share-settlement withholding, not a buyback). No combined figure published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 52/53-week year ending last Saturday of December (FY2025 ended 2025-12-27)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:03:33Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated the following Monday before the US open
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares 193.471M (basic cover count 192.910M at 2026-06-27); held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding) is fully expensed in the flows. The count has sat at 192-194M for a decade: RSU grants are offset by withholding, with no open-market programme in use.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.05 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.4% cost of equity; zero financial debt so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and Auto OEM programme risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases only (liability $210M at 2026-06-27, no finance leases, no borrowings). Lease cost is already inside operating expenses and operating cash flow, so it is charged through the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, consumer / cyclical'), 10-year horizon because capex and working capital are still normalising. Garmin is a Swiss-domiciled, NYSE-listed hardware company filing US GAAP in USD; adaptations read for the matching-asset rule and the charge-risk-once rule. INTEREST INCOME STRIPPED ($128.9M FY2025, 12.7x the owner-FCF base in net cash) and its source asset carried at fair value in the bridge: 'cash' = cash & equivalents $2,334.2M + available-for-sale securities current $332.0M + non-current $1,703.7M = $4,369.9M at 2026-06-27 (Q2 2026 10-Q, not yet in the SEC companyfacts index; read from the filing's inline XBRL). Total debt is zero. Owner FCF FY2025 = 1,362.9 reported FCF - 223.2 SBC incl. withholding - 128.9 interest income = 1,010.8 (13.9% of revenue); OCF less capex is the company's own FCF definition. EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC (FY2025: op income 1,876.1 + D&A 185.0 + SBC 166.0 = 2,227.1 = 30.7%); the engine deducts SBC separately. Working capital is modelled as a -30% capture on the revenue CHANGE: receivables + inventory ($3.1B) far exceed payables ($0.4B), and FY2023-25 OCF fell short of NI + D&A + SBC by $180-380M a year while revenue grew $370-1,020M. Guidance year FY2026: revenue ~$8.05B (+11.1%), GAAP operating margin ~27%, gross margin ~59.7%, 10% baseline tariff assumed; H1 2026 actual +12.7% revenue and 27.7% operating margin. Capex year 1 set at 4.5% (H1 2026 $194M vs $86M a year earlier) and tapers to 3.2%. Cash tax ramps 17% -> 18% (FY2025 cash taxes paid 15.7% of pre-tax, book ETR 17.4%; Swiss domicile under Pillar Two). Terminal cap 18x owner FCF for a consumer-hardware cyclical (15x in bear).

bear.narrative: H1 2026 is already booked (+12.7%), so FY2026 still grows ~9.5%, but the Fitness upgrade cycle exhausts itself in 2027 (Apple, Coros, Suunto and Chinese value wearables cap units), US tariffs on Taiwan-assembled goods step up beyond the 10% baseline and price increases dent demand, Marine and Aviation roll over with rate-sensitive boat and aircraft demand, and the Auto OEM gap between BMW roll-off and the Mercedes ramp widens. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin falls back to 27.5% (FY2022-23 territory) and the exit multiple compresses to 15x.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on raised guidance ($8.05B, 27% operating margin); Fitness decelerates from 25-40% to low-double-digit growth, Outdoor/Marine/Aviation grow mid-single-digit, Auto OEM dips in H2 2026 then recovers on the 2027 Mercedes-Benz programme. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin holds ~32% (tariffs at 10% and memory costs absorbed by mix and selective pricing). Capex normalises from the current facility build; working capital keeps consuming ~30 cents of every incremental revenue dollar.

bull.narrative: Fitness keeps compounding at 15-20% as health/AI-coaching features (CIRQA, Active Intelligence, Connect+, TrainingPeaks) pull Garmin from the athlete niche into mass-market wellness; Marine and Aviation stay double-digit; Mercedes-Benz ramps Auto OEM to profitability in 2027-28; tariffs stay at or below 10%. Recurring revenue and mix lift the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 34%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up because the single largest risk (US tariffs on Taiwan-assembled product, ~25% of revenue) is binary and outside management's control, and because FY2025-26 Fitness growth of 25-40% is unusual for hardware and can mean-revert quickly. Bull down because it needs three independent things to go right at once: sustained Fitness compounding, a benign tariff outcome and a profitable Mercedes-Benz ramp. The balance sheet ($4.4B cash and securities, no debt) removes any solvency tail, which is why bear is not higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
